Take Out Kitty Litter for Tyrone across the Vice City.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Taking Out Kitty Litter's lab locations in GTA 6 is a mission in Tyrone's questline, and sees you searching the city for 18 secret labs (after the first one he directs you to). Every lab has a red smoking chimney and a blue and white Spin On This laundry van parked outside.

It'll take a little while, but it's well worth it to get the unique gold SMG at the end. Plus, Tyrone will start buying narcotics from you for the highest price possible. To destroy each lab, simply shoot a smoking pink flask and then run away. I've also laid these out in the most optimal order, separated into regions, so you're not driving back and forth across Vice City.

Last note: if you want to unlock map markers for the labs yourself versus relying on these videos, you can threaten cooks in certain labs to potentially reveal them, or talk to Tyrone when you're fencing goods.

After you complete some missions for Tyrone (when you meet him with Dre'Quan during Dealer's Choice) he'll direct you to this trailer park in La Perle where you destroy the first Kitty Litter lab and start the hunt for the others. You can see the route to the lab in the video above.

You can find this one in the trailer park opposite Zenon's Pawn Shop Ammu-Nation in La Perle. As soon as you go through the main gate, you can see the trailer with the funnel chimney where they're cooking straight ahead. Sneak around the back and break inside to find the lab. Or take out the three guys in front and go in that way.

Just across the road from the Mezzasega Espresso and Slinger in the Decor District. Pull off to the right of the road into the Williams + Whitaker Homeware and Decor car park. You'll see a garage with a shutter at the far end with a smoking chimney and the laundry van parked. Open the shutter to find a lone guy in the lab.

This one is behind Peterson's Autoshop in Rockridge, directly south across the road from the Blessed Food Market, under the overpass, on the border between Rockridge and La Perle. Head through the main yard and turn left to spot the laundry van. Break into it, move it forward, and open the shutter behind to find the lab.

Just east of Fleeca Field stadium, next door to Xero Gas - Rockridge. You'll spot the blue and white laundry van parked off to the side of the road behind a wall. Head down that alley and turn right to find a garage door you can open with the lab inside.

On the east side of the condominium building directly south of the Vice City Hospital, by Emilio's Auto Center Gas. Look for the closed road with the laundry van parked at the southern end and some staircases and flats off to the side with the chimney spewing smoke. The lab is through the white door on the bottom floor.

Just down the road to the west of Bump and Grind coffee and Salon Belle, in a block of flats southeast of Fleeca Fields stadium. You can see the laundry van parked outside. The lab is on the upper floor on the left side in apartment 5, where you can see the smoking chimney. Break in via the front door to find the lab.

This lab is an easy one to find, around the back of Cross My Heart Tattoos. Head around the right side, turn left, and look to your left for the garage door with the guy sitting down guarding it, with the lab inside.

This lab is in the block of flats to the southeast of the Jack of Hearts and Urban Legendz, with the laundry van parked out front. Look inside apartment 103 on the first floor on the left side. It's quite hard to get away from this lab blowing up, so shoot it from outside and run away. Also this will likely cause a big shootout in the block, so book it.

This lab is to the southwest of your apartment in Chapter 3 and to the east of the Crosstown Mule - City Line marker. Look for an overgrown lot with the laundry van parked in it. The garage with the lab is just behind that.

This lab is directly west of Down Town Pawn, just between Rideout Customs and the Vargo's Gas station. Just past the gas station, look to the left where its fuel sign is to spot a laundry van, and further down the track, the garage with the lab and smoking chimney above it.

This lab is close to Xero Gas - Tequesta and west of Vice Seven Condominiums gym. When driving east to west past the station, turn right and keep an eye on your right towards the two floored condominiums for the laundry van parked outside. You want the set of staircases to the right of the van. Take the right side one up to the first floor to find the lab door directly ahead.

This lab is in a trailer park directly east down the road from Arrow Gas - VCIA, also west under the bridge from Pawn City and Vice City Firearms. Turn into the trailer park, take the first right and drive a little way around the corner to spot the trailer with the smoking chimney on the left. You can enter via a window around the other side to find the lab.

This lab is located in the far south of Salton, north of the Pay 'N' Spray - Salton, next door to the Slator Towing Inc robbery. Go around the south side of the derelict block of flats and climb the dumpster to jump up through the open window to find the lab.

This lab is west down the road from Xero Gas - Salton. Cross the train tracks, then keep an eye on your right for a carpark with a blue and white laundry van, then turn right into it to spot the building with the smoking chimney on the right. Hop the fence straight ahead and turn right to find one guy guarding the garage with the lab.

This lab is easy to find, directly south of Salon Perez and Safia Restaurant in Little Cuba. Look for some bungalows on the left with the laundry van parked outside. It's in the building with the chimney to the left of the one the van is parked in front of. The lab is the second door along.

This lab is north up the road from the Pay 'N' Spray - Balsero. Turn left down the alley with the laundry van parked to find a guy guarding the gate, a couple of guys inside, and the lab in an open garage further back behind them.

This lab is in a trailer park southeast from the Balasero jewelry stores, across the river. If driving from the east and the city, turn left before the bridge, turn right, then turn left and head a little way down to spot the trailer with the funnel chimney and laundry van outside. Sneak around back to get in and find the lab.

This lab is south across the river from Ron's Car Wash and Gas. Head over the bridge, across the junction, then keep an eye out to your left to spot where the laundry van is parked. The lab is just in the building beyond the gate with the smoking chimney. The door requires a code which is 1999 (referencing the billboard up to the right).

There are three main advantages to destroying all the Kitty Litter labs and completing the Spin On This mission with Tyrone and those are:

You'll also get $2,000 a lab, plus $10,000 for the Spin On This mission, meaning $48,000 altogether. Since I did everything, it's unclear to me whether these rewards are for destroying every lab, or the mission specifically that you get after you destroy 15 of them. Either way, if you want all of this, destroy all the labs in the city and complete the mission.

#3888. 13 arrested in Shanghai as police crackdown on bootleg Final Fantasy 7 Tifa figurine operation

Chinese police have arrested 13 individuals in Shanghai allegedly involved in a bootleg Final Fantasy 7 Tifa figurine business, after consumers reported the operation. They are currently being investigated on suspicion of selling infringing reproductions.

Reported by Gamespark, the police cracked down on the operation which involved the seizure of around $300,000 of goods related to the figurines.

The investigation started in May, after police received reports from concerned members of the public about the Tifa figurines. They were made from different materials than official figurines, and after confirming the illegitimacy of these products with the rights holders, Square Enix, police determined these businesses were not authorised to be producing such goods and went to work.

The appearance of these counterfeits were deemed identical to the real merch, and therefore the alleged crime was deemed infringement of official goods. These counterfeits also came in different sizes, some of which were more expensive than the originals and customisabile.

Looking at pictures taken by local outlet Shangguan News (and put side-by-side by Automaton), you can see the official Tifa figurine (right) next to the counterfeit version (left). Both show Tifa in a blue dress, though the materials used are clearly different.

#3887. Space station horror-FPS Derelikt is a lively retro throwback to Alien: Resurrection, though it's better at shooting than scaring

I'm a reasonable man. I don't expect every PS1-styled, cosmic horror, nakedly Alien: Resurrection-homaging retro FPS to suffocate me under a blanket of misery. Some of the lighter moments in Derelikt, which released last week, even land: I was grinning my cheeks off as I gorged on the Eldtrich knowledge sealed within an alien obelisk, while repeatedly hanging up on the aghast scientist who kept videocalling me to stop.

Still, Derelikt is fortunate that it's a good shooter, as it often gets muddled on whether it wants to be a horror game as well. It certainly threatens the spooks, trapping you in an oppressively dingy asteroid rig in the orbit of Saturn - the scariest of the ringed gas giants! - and warping most of the other staff into vaguely echinodemic monsterpeople. Also, opening the inventory reveals it to be made of rectangles, a classic symptom of a video game character about to get mangled in the nerves and face.

But nah, shotgun go boom boom. It turns out Derelikt's derelict dwellers are both perfectly susceptible to mundane lead, and sparing users of ambush tactics at most; several even stand around with their backs turned, as if waiting for you to surprise them with a lethal pipe swing. And, even on Medium difficulty, the opening spell of fight-or-run scarcity quickly gives way to an abundance of ammo and health pickups that can easily fill the pocket grid to bursting. I don't claim to have been playing perfectly, but I'm about halfway through and the only way I see myself running low on bullets is if I start using them to punch the complete works of Thomas Campion into a wall.

It's indecisive tonally, as well. The dialogue, and there are a fair few survivors to chat with, seems interested in emulating the gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style of New Millennium action game scripts. Which I can sort of see the logic behind, given the visuals and sound design also, and arguably much more painstakingly, mimic that era. But the downside remains that it ends up with a gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style, just with an extra dash of sideways-winking awareness. Again, it only sometimes works, and it's never scary or eerie. But then there are also more earnest attempts to spin uneasiness, with pages of deranged scribbles left behind by the dwindling crew, and at least a couple of genre-classic wall daubings, which tend to leave me wishing developers Visuwyg had just picked a lane.

Again, though, underneath all the smartarsing is a quality little shooter. The retro presentation does little to soften the heavy, industrial kick of its gunfire, and although many of the meatier freaks are more absorbent than they look, their pained thrashing really helps sell the impact of every individual shot. I also don't really mind the lack of Dead Spacey surprise attacks, as the station's narrow confines tend to force you into tenser, close-range encounters in an organic way anyhow.

More impressive still is how Derelikt manages to fabricate a cold, apprehensive atmosphere befitting its fallen space base, in direct defiance of its own quasi-comedic script. This is mainly thanks to the clanging, low-lit station itself, which teases you with just enough flashes of comfort – a stretch of marble floor here, a messy rec room there – to make your quick return to its steel guts feel all the more unpleasant. Some credit must also go to the puzzling, the cardkey hunts and code searches of which initially had me fearful of the more obstinate, opaque, classic horror style preferred by fellow backwards-looker Silver Pines. Instead, it's more like a compacted Deus Ex, hinting at the need to peek at people's computers and scour the environments for the needed codes. Which makes for generally smoother progress, yes, but also gets you more involved and present inside Derelikt's infested walls.

Midway-through impressions, then: it's a little silly, and perhaps a little confused, but Derelikt finds its focus whenever something needs making dead. I shall continue blasting xenos and burning my eyes out with magic rocks until – no, madam, please hold – further notice.

#3886. PS Plus Essential's Next Update Looks a Bit Better in Japan Than the Rest of the World

It’s all subjective, of course, but Japan’s PS Plus Essential update for December 2026 looks a little bit better than what we’re getting in the west.

Now if we’re looking at pure value here, the Japanese lineup is objectively better: the Bleach game retails for $59.99, while Amnesia is $24.99. The former is also available on PS5 and PS4, whereas the latter is only available for PS4 (although you can of course play it on PS5 via backwards compatibility).

Bleach is also newer, having released in 2025, while Amnesia is from 2023.

But it does ultimately all come down to taste, I suppose; survival horror fans may be much happier with Frictional’s title – especially if they have no real interest in anime. I suppose the lineup in Japan does lack variety, as you’re getting two very similar titles from Bandai Namco there.

Amnesia: The Bunker did release in Japan, so I’m not entirely sure why the lineup is different between regions.

Sony is putting a lot of marketing into its domestic region at the moment, as it tries to reverse its flagging fortunes. It’s also just launched a new PS Portal there, and is putting a pretty big promotional campaign behind it. Maybe it thinks this lineup will be more enticing to Japanese players.

Interesting stuff, though, which selection would you have preferred? I’ve had the Bleach game on my wishlist for a little while, so I think I would have rather got that – but I can certainly see why people would prefer the more varied worldwide selection as well.

EA has always been "so resistant" to remake or remaster its games, says Mark Darrah

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The premature death of BioWare is made even sadder by the fact that many of its best games were never remastered or remade for modern hardware, and now they probably never will be. Compare that to an RPG studio like Bethesda, which is notorious for endlessly remastering, re-releasing, and porting The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim, and it's easy to see why BioWare diehards feel like they were dealt a bad hand by the studio's parent company, EA.

Not to rub salt into the wound, but former Dragon Age lead Mark Darrah, a BioWare veteran who worked at the studio for more than two decades, Dragon Age: Origins could've easily been remastered and probably would've sold pretty well if it weren't for EA's reluctance to remake or remaster anything.

Talking to Pembridge TV (timestamp), Darrah says a big reason EA doesn't typically modernize its older games is because a big portion of its IP catalog is annual sports games like EA Sports FC and NHL. "What are you gonna take NHL 2005 and do a 20th anniversary remaster? What? You have an NHL. NHL never went away. Madden never went away. Football Club never went away," Darrah says.

That doesn't explain why series like Mass Effect and Dragon Age didn't get more remasters (on that, Darrah simply says "they don't get it"), but Darrah says the opportunity was there even if Skyrim levels of ports wouldn't work.

"Honestly, yeah, I don't know that anyone other than Bethesda could get away with porting Skyrim to every single platform and selling a million copies every single time they do that," he says, adding, "But yes! We could have remastered Origins probably twice and sold a couple million copies each time."

Nobody wants to work for their crimes anymore, smh.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It's come to my attention that some of us aren't having a very fun time with the NPCs in Grand Theft Auto 6. I've seen videos and threads of players complaining about not being able to steal cars because of crack head drivers, getting hunted down by killer NPCs, and just generally having a harder time traversing Leonida because who knows what bloodthirsty beast hides behind each corner? And to this I say, your steak is too buttery? Your lobster too juicy?

My first interaction with one of the unfriendly residents of Leonida started when I accidentally bumped into their car. Because I am wholly unaware of my surroundings, I didn't even notice that anyone was mad at me as I listened to my pop songs and carried on driving towards my mission. Little did I know that right behind me was a four-wheeler with a driver who had steam coming out of her ears.

So I pull up to the side of the road, ready to head in and start my mission, when seemingly out of nowhere the four-wheeler comes barreling in, almost taking me out completely. The driver gets out and starts screaming about payback. I have no idea what I've done, but this is GTA 6, I'm not taking this slander. So I start swinging.

The fight ends with me knocking this lady out, but she doesn't go down without a fight. At one point, I actually thought that was it for me—taken out on the pavement by a soccer mum, what a way to go.

But even if I had taken a long sleep on the sidewalk, that would've been OK, because it's all part of the beautiful package that GTA 6 offers.

I don't want vapid NPCs that buckle at the first sight of a handgun, or have the object permanence of a goldfish. Filling Leonida with some actually competent, and dare I say dangerous NPCs makes this game infinitely more interesting. I like not knowing how one small action will ruin my whole day, or having to be a little wary of the people around me lest I want to incur a murderous chase across the city streets.

Terrorising helpless NPCs is fun, but only for a short while.

I have a theory as to why players are pushing back against aggressive NPCs: they just don't like having to put in the effort after years of being able to do whatever they want in GTA Online. There's certainly some that will look back on the mostly timid NPCs of Los Santos and miss when all they had to do to steal a car was swing open its door and throw the limp driver out. Aside from shouting, there wasn't really anything a regular NPC could do to pose a threat to you back then.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Rockstar amped up the mayhem and carnage you could cause, turning it into a chaotic playground with few repercussions. GTA Online players have become accustomed to walking around like some vengeful god, wreaking havoc wherever or whenever they see fit, and only very occasionally dealing out mercy. Now these fickle deities have been forced to become human again.

A part of me understands the appeal. Terrorising helpless NPCs is fun, but only for a short while. NPCs that actually have a backbone offer an experience that will keep me interested for far longer.

Plus, Leonida is based on Florida, do you honestly think you could terrorise the streets of Miami or Tampa Bay and walk out completely unscathed? Yeah, I thought as much.

#3883. Valve are pausing Steam Machine 2TB orders over "supply constraints," though the 512GB model is free of its waitlist

Valve giveth, and Valve taketh away in their latest Steam Machine availability update. The dinky SteamOS PC continues to have a terrible time with AI industry-inflicted hardware parts shortages, which at least for its flagship 2TB model, have become such a problem that Valve are suspending new orders until further notice. While Valve's post says that they "have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders" – meaning if you'd previously reserved one, you'll still get your chance to buy – "supply restraints" have put the kibosh on any new orders for now.

It's not all bad news, though. The cheaper 512GB Steam Machine has achieved "add-to-cart status", which is Valve's slightly odd way of saying you can snap one up without having to join a reservation waitlist. Just like in the Before Times! The post does add that 512GB stock is still limited, so that might sell out too if they can't source enough parts to build new ones, though this is still the first time that the refreshed Steam Machine has been waitlist-free since launching in June.

One could, with the aid of a Torx screwdriver and a conveniently illustrated guide, work around the 2TB model's lack of existence by nabbing a readily available 512GB Machine and replacing its stock SSD with a chunkier aftermarket drive. A not-terrible, budget two-gigster can be had from £240, which when added to the 512GB Machine's £879 outlay, actually works out a little less than buying a 2TB Machine as is. SteamOS is free to download and install, and swapping out the Steam Machine's SSD is considerably easier than the plasticky brain surgery of Steam Deck drive replacement.

Of course, ideally none of that would be necessary, and we could all fill our living rooms with sub-£700 Steam Machines that had never been choked by the greedy hands of industrial-scale RAM hoarders. But that's not the world we live in. Indeed, Valve end the post by rather chillingly suggesting that their hardware prices may rise yet again.

"We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units," they say, "but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them. The 2TB model in particular will be especially constrained."

"We anticipate having more information to share come January."

#3882. Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang accused of decades of bullying and workplace abuse in new investigation

Public humiliation reportedly considered a "rite of passage".

An investigation into the workplace behavior of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who resigned recently after a series of extramarital affairs came to light, has uncovered decades of harassment, verbal employee abuse and "cultish" behaviour at the company which has long played a major role in PC gaming.

Following Huang's departure, The New York Times has published a report in which "more than a dozen" current and former Nvidia employees discussed their experiences with the former CEO. Speaking on conditions of anonymity, employees alleged Jensen Huang would verbally berate them, reportedly going as far as to say he'd rip their arms off, rip their heart out and stomp on it, or rip their head off and "pee on your brain".

The report includes numerous examples of Huang's alleged abusive behaviour, which apparently stretches back years before Nvidia became the one of the most valuable companies in the world - years before the AI boom. It's claimed Huang on one occasion went around a room of managers telling them he'd kill them. Then, when he reached a person in their 70s, said everyone hoped they'd drop dead.

Huang allegedly referred to these bouts of public humiliation as a "rite of passage" at Nvidia, when questioned by an internal HR employee whom he later fired for not being a "right fit". Huan's stance was apparently to test whether a person could handle the culture there, which is described in the report as "cultish".

It's claimed Huang's influence at Nvidia has meant other senior managers have followed his lead, including his daughter Madison, Nvidia's chief of staff, who it's said often yells at staff, including executives more highly ranked than her.

A spokesperson for Huang denied the allegations in response to a request for comment by the New York Times. The spokesperson, John Fisher, said the claims in the report were "fabrications that are now impossible to disprove specifically, and the thousands of Nvidia employees who continue to speak out for Jensen show they’re false".

Huang resigned from his role as Nvidia CEO earlier this month after a series of extramarital affairs were unearthed - one with a person US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy, and two others with Nvidia employees. The chair of Nvidia's board, Harvey C. Jones, reportedly said earlier this week that the company "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".

#3881. The Witcher 3 Remastered Patch 5.02 Fixes Annoying PS5 Stutters, Improves Performance, and Much More

The Witcher 3 Remastered has a new update on PS5, and it's available to download right now, weighing in at a reasonable 1.6GB.

Patch 5.02 is the one many have been waiting for, as it addresses the game's most annoying technical issue on console. I am, of course, referring to the momentary stutters that occurred when autosave was triggered.

This problem was especially noticeable when quest information popped up on the screen, both when you began a quest and finished it. Thankfully, CD Projekt Red's finally taken action.

The patch also improves v-sync and VRR "behaviour" on PS5, which should result in a smoother overall experience. Screen flickering has also been addressed.

On top of those more-than-welcome adjustments, the update is packed with bug fixes — some of which are related to the remaster's new lighting techniques, which could result in some areas looking poorly or incorrectly illuminated.

And in terms of gameplay, we're looking at a bunch of balancing tweaks to a number of Geralt's skills. Some of these perks simply weren't being calculated properly, so you should be more effective in combat right out of the gate with this update installed.

Sam Corcos is vibe-coding Legatum, a "historical 4X on a hex map, built for people who love Civilization"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

While DOGE itself is long dead, some of the officials appointed by the Elon Musk-backed organization remain part of the United States government. That includes Sam Corcos, who joined the Treasury Department as special advisor in 2025 and soon became chief information officer there. Corcos remains in that position amid a heavily scrutinized cybersecurity breach at the department, but that hasn't stopped him from finding the time to continue vibe-coding his Civilization clone.

Yes, Corcos is creating a game, in the loosest terms, called Legatum, which is a "historical 4X on a hex map, built for people who love Civilization." Taking specific inspiration from Civilization 6, it's "familiar on purpose," according to the GitHub readme, letting you choose a civilization and build alliances or make war on rivals as progress through nine eras and try to build the greatest empire of all.

"Legatum is built largely with AI coding agents, and all of its art is AI-generated," that readme explains. "Most of the art comes from OpenAI's image models through ChatGPT; the icons and heraldry are SVG drawn by scripts in this repository. The working files are public so that other people can learn from them."

Dozens upon dozens of updates have been made to Legatum in the past few days, a fact that has drawn some scrutiny given that the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, a bureau of the Treasury Department, is in the midst of dealing with a self-described "cybersecurity incident."

A notice on FinCEN's website notes that the breach has "resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems. As a proactive measure, FinCEN has taken some systems offline." While few details on this incident have been made public, a breach of a US bureau dedicated to fighting financial crime does seem like an 'all hands on deck' situation that would give the organization's CIO something more important to do.

For his part, Corcos tweets that "the computers are doing it on their own. Mostly Opus 5.5 orchestrating a bunch of iterative loops." But, as 404 Media notes, he's finding time to regularly give feedback to Claude on new features and tweaks that should be made for Legatum.

Using GitHub's issue tracker, users have noted a problem with the code: "Treasury CIO is too busy vibecoding instead of doing his job." Several comments seem to agree, but Corcos eventually closed the discussion as "off-topic," since the "tracker is for bugs and ideas about the Legatum game." This response was also generated by Claude.

Four years ago (oh my god) strategy RPG Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga rather impressed our reviewer Jon Bolding. He wrote that "novel tactical mechanics make this indie a contender for the best strategy RPG this year".

Well, buckle up, 2027, because Symphony of War 2 has broken cover with a promise to release next year, and it's coming courtesy of the strategy sommeliers at publisher Hooded Horse, which I take as a very good sign.

SOW2 looks set to continue the Fire-Emblem-ish framework of its predecessor, tasking you with recruiting a gaggle of heroes to wage war with (and possibly compose symphonies, who's to say?) in "a world filled with political intrigue, betrayal, and tense, large-scale tactical battles". Which is a lot like our world, really.

It all looks very nice indeed. In the announcement trailer, we get glimpses of its squad-based combat and anime cutscenes, and I am officially into both. The art is poppy and distinctive, at some point an age-of-sail warship transforms into some kind of German WW1 destroyer, and the overworld triggers the regions in my brain devoted to thinking about Heroes of Might and Magic. Check, check, and check.

"Anime cutscenes!?" I hear you cry. "That sounds like the kind of thing that bespeaks a dense tapestry of lore I'll need to get to grips with first!" Well, apparently not. I am informed by Symphony of War 2's Steam page that the devs have no expectation you know what a "Nephilim Saga" even is before you pick this game up. "Symphony of War 2 is a standalone experience set several generations after the events of the first game—it can be enjoyed without having played Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga". The game's tale of a fallen empire trying to un-fall can be enjoyed single-serve.

#3878. GTA 6 leaker claims to have lobbed a near-complete Xbox build of Rockstar's crimsim onto the net, shouts that the "community will have it emulated inside a week"

Cyberleek, the GTA 6 leaker or leakers who shared a bunch of alleged gameplay earlier this year, are now claiming to have released a nearly complete in-development build of the crimsim's Xbox version. Continuing their established grift, the leaker or leakers are threatening to release the main executable file they've withheld unless people pump up the value of their cryptocurrency.

"It is done," a statement posted on Cyberleek’s website claimed. "CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto VI, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one - the main executable - held on a countdown. Honest terms, as always: it is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons."

So, more anime villain chatter from Cyberleek, who claim the executable file is on a timer and will be released immediately if their crypto coin reaches a $15 million market cap. It looks like the build is yet to be confirmed as genuine.

If any build leak were to result in GTA 6 being emulated on PC in rapid fashion, that would threaten to undercut an official port. Rockstar have yet to confirm that such a port is on the way and when it'll drop, but an October report from GamesBeat claimed the first three months of 2027 as the window in which Rockstar plan to deliver the game to PC. Former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij recently told our Edwin he reckons that concerns about unofficial ports based on the console version of GTA 6, likely made with generative AI, might lead Rockstar not to leave too big a gap before bringing the crimsim to PC officially.

Any alleged playable unofficial port of GTA 6 made with help from genAI and chucked online could, of course, just be a great big pile of malware.

Rockstar, who previously called the initial barrage of leaks laid claim to by Cyberleek "heartbreaking", as well as parent company Take-Two, looked to have begun a hunt for the identity of the leakers back in August.

#3877. GTA 6 credits actually include 'Florida Joker', the viral internet personality who once demanded $10 million from Rockstar Games

Lawrence Sullivan, better known to the online world as the 'Florida Joker', is in GTA 6. After accusing Rockstar Games of using his likeness without consent and then demanding a $10m payout, the two parties have seemingly settled their differences.

Grand Theft Auto 6's earliest controversy came from its very first official trailer, when Sullivan alleged one of the teaser's similarly tattooed characters was modeled after him. The former tattoo model, who first went viral because of a mugshot that shared an uncanny resemblance to Batman's Joker, soon called on Rockstar to pay him $2m. His demand quickly shot up to $10m, before he dropped all legal threats and politely asked to officially work with the developer.

Rockstar seems to have relented to that last request - the vast GTA 6 credits include none other than one Lawrence Sullivan, listed under the 'Local Population' cast, alongside dozens of other names.

GTA 6 players wasted no time, and quickly found the suspect first teased way back in that original 2023 trailer. In its quest to parody all parts of modern life under capitalism, GTA 6 lets you doomscroll through a social media app called Snapmatic, which flings an endless number of short-form clips and thirst traps at you. If you're lucky enough, or if you scroll for long enough, you'll find a video of Sullivan's in-game counterpart beating up a fake lookalike. He certainly sounds like Sullivan, too.

"Two years y'all been talking crazy about me," he wrote under a recent Instagram post. "Who got the last laugh now?!"

The GTA 6 credits were illuminating for other reasons, too. We finally know who voices the game's loveable duo, Jason and Lucia, for one. All 34 of the infamously fired Rockstar workers also appear in GTA 6's credits. The controversial move eventually led to accusations of union busting on Rockstar's part, which is currently being investigated as part of an employment tribunal in Scotland.

The true box office winner of Dunesday has been predicted by the Nielsen ratings, and it's none other than Avengers: Doomsday.

Per Deadline, NRG (National Research Group, owned by Nielsen) predicts that Doomsday will bring in $270 million at the global box office during its opening weekend. Dune 3 is predicted to bring in $75 million.

This is the highest projection NRG has ever recorded, with Spider-Man: Brand New Day being the second-highest. To date, Avengers: Endgame now holds the record second-highest opening weekend for any movie ever at $357.1M, having been beat out by Spider-Man: Brand New Day's $360 million.

Avengers: Doomsday tickets went on sale back in July for the special Infinity Vision screenings. It's worth noting that 60,000 more tickets were sold for the early Thursday screenings following the VisionQuest finale, which teases the return of Wanda Maximoff aka the Scarlet Witch. Wanda will indeed return in Doomsday, but she won't be, uh, herself... if you catch my drift.

Dune 3 tickets have been a bit of a nightmare for fans as they sold out almost immediately back in April, and then crashed several movie theater apps when more tickets were released back in August. Oh, and, when tickets did sell out in April... people started reselling them for up to $1000. The people yearn for sand.

Avengers: Doomsday and Dune 3 hit theaters on December 18. For more on the MCU, check out our guide to the Marvel timeline and how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

#3875. Amid a year of layoffs, Ubisoft yank the cover off Motherbrain, their new studio "focused on AI for gameplay innovation"

Something something "proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators" something something

Ubisoft have revealed their Motherbrain. It's far less cool than it sounds. Rather than being a giant floating slab of thinky meat that can do telepathy, Motherbrain is a studio dedicated to doing development stuff with generative AI. As you might expect, it consists of the folks who worked on Ubisoft's "first playable generative AI experience".

Motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the company trumpeted that their "new operating model" is "now fully in place". The model is the reorganising into creative houses responsible for different game series that Ubisoft announced at the start of this year, with leaders for all of the houses now arranged.

"We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up new possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot said.

You'll never guess what his next few lines were. "We remain on track with our cost reduction program, reflecting our commitment to a focused and disciplined organization as we are preparing for a significantly stronger content cycle," the exec said. "In parallel, we have made progress on our refinancing plan with the objective of securing competitive terms and putting in place an efficient medium-term plan over the coming months."

That'd be the wave of layoffs and closures Ubisoft have been rolling out all through this year, most recently getting rid of 166 staff at Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, both of which worked on Assassin's Creed Shadows. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx, Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona, long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm, Ubisoft's Paris HQ and three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz are all on the list of bits of the company affected in some way by the cuts.

Changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

Ah well, at least there's seemingly money there to support the developing of those proprietary technologies infused with genAI brainiacery.

#3874. After taking seven years to make Persona 6 and four years to make Persona 5, Atlus promises future games will come quicker

"People won't have to wait as long for the next game as they have previously."

Persona 6 is still slowly chugging in the background, but developer Atlus is promising that future games in its beloved RPG series won't take quite as long as they used to.

There was a four year gap between 2012's Persona 4 Golden and the original Persona 5, and it's already been seven years since the expanded Persona 5 Royal first dropped. Despite the sometimes agonising wait filled with countless spin-offs and collaborations with live service games, we've only seen a vague teaser trailer for the next proper Persona.

P-Studio general producer Kazuhisa Wada recently assured folks that the pattern wouldn't repeat again. "Persona 6 is not the end," he said in a Sega Samania interview translated by GamesRadar. "We have been working to make sure that people won't have to wait as long for the next game as they have previously. In order for Persona to grow as an IP, we consider how to live up to people's expectations in terms of creativity and development every day."

Wada doesn't go into any more detail about how Atlus plans to release Persona games quicker. Is the next mainline game already in development alongside Persona 6, or is Atlus just streamlining how it makes games? Either way, the studio seems to have abandoned its divisive habit of returning to and improving its games after a few years - P3 Portable, P4 Golden, P5 Royal. I imagine that'll cut down on wait times, at least somewhat.

"Large-scale RPGs like the Persona series take five years or more to develop," he added. "So there can be a long time between numbered entries."

As for Persona 6 itself, Wada unsurprisingly "can't say much" about the much-hyped, high-schooling, demon-punching game. "But we want our games to demonstrate all of the hard work we've put in. With that in mind, we are creating something better than anything we've made before, and that is hugely satisfying."

We don't know much about Atlus' occult sequel, officially, but a massive information leak earlier in the year revealed a full achievement list for Persona 6 and a bunch of other unreleased games, including Kingdom Hearts 4 and an unannounced Sea of Thieves project. Be wary of online spoilers, then.

#3873. GTA 6 Gives PS5 a Very Rare Win Over Switch 2 in Japan

At this point, it’s well known that Switch 2 is by far the market leader in Japan.

While the PS5 still commands some marketshare, it gets dominated by the Nintendo machine on a weekly basis.

GTA 6’s launch is significant, then, because for the first time in a while it’s pushed Sony’s console in front of the Switch 2 – albeit only by a few thousand units.

According to Famitsu’s latest report, the PS5 sold 41,472 units through the week ending 22nd November, while the Switch 2 managed 36,817 units.

This is an incredibly rare scenario, and likely won’t be repeated again (if ever). But it shows that with the right software, Sony can put up a fight domestically against Nintendo.

The company’s been taking the region a lot more seriously under Japanese CEO Hideaki Nishino, launching more affordable region locked units to try and stimulate interest.

This week saw the release of the new Midnight Black model, which certainly helped contribute to the sales.

But PS5’s success was primarily motivated by GTA 6, which sold a very respectable 200,759 units at retail for the week.

That’s slightly less than GTA 5’s 304,752 units opening in 2013, although remember digital buying habits have changed dramatically in the last 13 years, and GTA 6’s physical release was not particularly compelling as it doesn’t include a disc.

A good week for Sony in its home region, then – one that’s unlikely to be replicated, but should be taken as a sign it can compete with the right lineup and pricing model.

Ken Kutaragi says the Microsoft boss he met "was so arrogant"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Ken Kutaragi led the development of Sony's video game consoles for years, and is widely known as "the father of the PlayStation." As it turns out, he might also be the father of the Xbox – or, at least, its distant uncle. In a new interview, Kutaragi claims to have been playing 4D chess in a meeting with a Microsoft executive, essentially tricking the company into creating its own game console.

"I had the chance to meet with the head of Microsoft one-to-one," Kutaragi tells The Game Business. The literal head of Microsoft in this era would, of course, have been Bill Gates, though Kutaragi isn't specific about who specifically he spoke to. Whoever it was, he wasn't terribly impressed: "He was so arrogant."

"Sony has no money, but they have huge money," Kutaragi continues. He showed this Microsoft executive what Sony was developing, and got an offer in return, where Microsoft would send "free hard disk drives to Sony" if they would, in exchange, "give some license rights" to Microsoft. "He tried to convince me," Kutaragi claims.

"I said only one word: 'No,'" he says. "'No thanks.' I was not so super arrogant as they were. I had a dream. If I say 'no,' they will get started on bringing in another platform after PC. That was my secret intention. They did, spending huge money on it."

The exact timeline here is unclear – Kutaragi doesn't specify whether it was the PS1 or the PS2 that he was quietly showing to Microsoft. Either way, by 2001, Microsoft had launched its own game console, the Xbox, as a direct competitor to PS2. Notably, one of the Xbox's key differentiators was its built-in hard drive, which may have been on the table for PS2 if Kutaragi hadn't shut Microsoft's offer down. Not that Sony had much reason to worry, since PS2 still outsold Xbox by several orders of magnitude.

Still, the rivalry between PlayStation and Xbox would drive the console market forward for many years to follow. "We, together, opened up this field," Kutaragi says. "That was very intentional."

#3870. GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-sale copies and a bonkers $3.79 billion in its first day

"We are incredibly humbled by the response."

Surprise, surprise - GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, surpassing its predecessor's 13-year-long record and the already optimistic analyst estimates.

Rockstar Games today confirmed that its cultural juggernaut sold a staggering 32.5 million pre-release copies across PS5 and Xbox Series X/S before its official worldwide launch on the 19th of November. By the end of its first day on sale, GTA 6 managed to rake in a frankly absurd $3.79bn. Not a bad haul.

As Rockstar was quick to brag, the whopping performance means GTA 6 set "a new record for entertainment across any medium" by "becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history."

For context, GTA 5 made around $800m in its opening 24 hours more than a decade ago. That mammoth debut almost looks quaint next to GTA 6's stunning numbers, although it's notable GTA 5 didn't launch immediately in Japan or Brazil - GTA 6 is available in almost every market with access to PlayStation and Xbox consoles.

"It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI," said Rockstar co-founder and company president, Sam Houser, in a recent press release. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn't be more excited to share this moment with you."

Previous estimates guessed that GTA 6 had sold almost 25m copies ($2.5bn in revenue) on day one. It's fair to say the game's staggering performance blew even those sky-high projections out of the water.

Every early indicator pointed to GTA 6's inevitably record-breaking launch. Parent company Take-Two previously said the game was tracking "well above expectations," as the crime fest sold more pre-orders than any other game in PlayStation Store and Xbox Store history.

The only question now is whether GTA 6 can ever outsell GTA 5's mammoth 230m copies, which it reached thanks to a very healthy cadence of GTA Online updates. How high GTA 6 can go will likely depend on its multiplayer offering, though Rockstar hasn't said anything concrete about that just yet.

"A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that," Chris Tapsell gushed in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

#3869. Akira Kurabayashi, company director at Arika and developer on Street Fighter EX, Tetris 99, Fighting EX Layer and more, has sadly passed away due to heart failure

As announced in a statement by Arika president Akira Nishitani (and translated by Time Extension, thank you), Akira Kurabayashi, a director at the combined dev/publishing studio and a creator whose work spans three decades and several genres, sadly passed away as a result of heart failure late last week.

Kurabayashi initially worked as a programmer on smaller titles at Taito, including early 2.5D fighting game Fighters' Impact (later localised as VS. in America). He then moved to Arika in 1996 and continued his work in 2.5D fighters with the Street Fighter EX series, a subseries which took the originator of the fighting game genre into the third dimension for the first time. While that subseries didn't last long, its spiritual successor Fighting EX Layer made waves in 2018, bringing back original characters from SFEX and even including Fatal Fury's Terry Bogard.

Fighting EX Layer started out as an April Fools' joke back in 2017, but the reaction to the trailer from fans who missed the SFEX series convinced Arika to bring the series back, even without the Capcom IP. The final result is an interesting 2.5D fighter that combines conventional mechanics, such as magic series combos and supers, with the unique (for better and worse) Gougi system, where of in-match perks are chosen from a deck of cards at roundstart. I had a good time playing it for its systems (and Terry is very fun in it), but the Gougi system brought to mind Street Fighter x Tekken's infamous paid Gem debacle, which no one should be reminded of. Anyway. In addition to 2.5D fighters, Kurabayashi also contributed to Tetris: The Grandmaster, Tetris 99, PAC-MAN 99, and ARIKA's collaboration with SNK in the form of their 'SNK Revamp Project'.

Nishitani gave a few personal words towards Kurabayashi in the statement:

"We are deeply saddened to have lost a dear colleague who has created numerous works with us and supported Arika for many years. We express our heartfelt respect and gratitude for his immense achievements to date, and we will cherish and carry on the skills, experience, and attitude toward game development that he left behind. I would like to express my deepest gratitude for the kindness you showed us during their lifetime, and I respectfully pray for the repose of their soul."

The leads of Leonida, the biggest and best-known effort to recreate GTA 6 on PC, have quit the project, although others are still trying to carry it on.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Just a day after Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek released the executable for the near-complete Xbox build of the game they dropped on Friday, at least two of the leads of Leonida, the biggest and best-known effort to recompile it to run on PC, have called it quits—seemingly under pressure from Take-Two and Rockstar.

The release of the exe made the pirated Xbox build effectively complete, and that opened the door for recomp projects to do their thing—that is, to leverage AI to quickly whip up a version of the game that will run on PC. Some hackers estimated it could be done within a week; Shayder, one of the lead developers on the Leonida project, said on X that followers could "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon."

In a separate message on the Leonida Discord, Shayder tempered expectations a bit, writing that "it will take at least a week" to come up with something playable on PC. During a subsequent livestream, however, the team was seemingly able to get the GTA 6 splash screen to come up on PC, although it crashed after that. It sure seemed like things were moving ahead quickly.

But then things began moving quickly in a different direction. "I quit guys. I’m sorry," NotRexed, apparently the head of the project, posted last night on X. "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can’t control so I’m stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity."

Later, they added, "Last post from me. I wanna clear things up. Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I’ve said before, I’m a 15 year old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye."

In a reply post, NotRexed stated explicitly that "Rockstar shut the server down," and shared an image of the copyright violation notice he'd received from Discord.

Shayder, who had previously predicted rapid progress on the Leonida effort following the release of the Xbox executable, took a more direct approach and simply deleted all of their X posts.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

This isn't necessarily the end of work to bring GTA 6 (in a probably not-great state) to PC via AI. Other such projects are underway, and there also appears to be an effort to carry on with Leonida: The website remains up, with a new name attached as owner, and there's at least one Discord server dedicated to it, although it appears a little less focused at this point than the original Leonida server. A new Github repository (NotRexed also deleted that) has been set up: It's "a continuation of NotRexed's Leonida project," according to a note on the project, which adds that "development continues here with its full commit history."

The advent of AI greatly simplifies and speeds up the work of bringing console games to PC (as long as you're not too picky about the quality), and that makes life tougher for companies that want to keep a lid on such projects. Still, it's not surprising that Take-Two and Rockstar are going hard on it: In the past, Take-Two has moved aggressively to shut down GTA 5 mod projects, an effort that culminated in its acquisition of the biggest and best of them. I've reached out to Take-Two for more information on the takedown and will update if I receive a reply.

#3867. GTA 6 features the series' first non-binary character, says actor Jesse James Rose, and players can't hurt them

Grand Theft Auto 6 features the first non-binary character in the series' history, according to actor Jesse James Rose, who plays the role of a museum curator in the game.

"I can FINALLY share that I play the first-ever nonbinary character in the Grand Theft Auto franchise!" Rose wrote on Instagram.

"Absolutely wild to find out THIS was the super-secret game I spent weeks and 17 NDAs filming 3 years ago."

"I shot this back in my they/them days, and everyone on production ensured I was comfortable and gendered correctly," Rose wrote. The project was kept so secret that Rose wasn't told what it was during filming and only recently learned it was GTA 6.

"GTA was one of the most inclusive & caring sets I've ever been on," they added.

A post shared by Jesse James Rose ✨ (@jamesissmiling)

The role was shot entirely through motion capture, which meant wearing "a unitard made of dots every day". Rose also says steps were taken to protect the character in-game: "To mitigate anti-trans violence, I was assured that players would not be able to inflict violence against my character."

A whole day of the shoot was spent scanning Rose's face, including hours of pulling different expressions. At one point Rose couldn't move a particular muscle, and worried the scan had been ruined, but the director was thrilled.

"That right there is exactly why we'll never use AI," he said, according to Rose. "A computer could never come up with the face you just made."

"Remember, in a world consumed with Generative AI, the largest video game in history chose human labour to preserve the integrity of the game," Rose added.

Rose did raise some concerns about pay, though.

"Despite being paid well for my time on set, I'll never see a residual check for my work," Rose wrote, explaining that this is part of SAG’s contract with game developers. As a union leader at one of SAG's sister unions, Rose said there's still "a long way to go to ensure arts workers are fairly compensated for our labour".

Rose also says many other trans people worked on GTA 6, both in front of the camera and behind it. "SO many trans people besides me are featured in GTA VI as other roles, designers, writers, etc... take a note, theatre and TV! We are employable & profitable!!!"

Finally, Rose voiced support for Rockstar's UK staff. "UK-based workers at Rockstar Games are currently voting on whether to unionise, and I sincerely hope their efforts are successful," Rose wrote. "Every arts worker should have a stable job with benefits and fair working conditions protected by a union."

GTA 6 is out now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It launched on Thursday, although some have been getting in on the action earlier, as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even New Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first."

"And then Obsidian was like, 'we'll try'"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

BioWare made one of the most beloved RPGs of all time with Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, but it was Obisidan that followed up with Knights of the Old Republic 2: The Sith Lords, another massively popular game. It's somewhat well-documented that publisher LucasArts wanted the sequel done quickly and that BioWare turned down the project for that reason, but in a new interview, BioWare veteran John Winski confirms that's the case and even puts an exact number on LucasArts' request.

Talking to Pembridge TV, Winski says LucasArts approached BioWare to develop Knights of the Old Republic 2 and asked for the project to be completed in just 18 months. "When LucasArts came to us and said, 'hey, you want to make a sequel?' We were like, 'OK,' and they gave us 18 months, and we were like, 'nope. No. We can't do it in 18 months. That's not enough time'," says Winski. "And then Obsidian was like, 'we'll try.'"

Try, Obsidian did, and for the most part, it succeeded. Winski rightfully points out Knights of the Old Republic 2 was released in a pretty sorry state, or in his words, not "totally finished," but he acknowledges that "a lot of people really love it" despite an "unreasonable" development cycle set by LucasArts. "It's still something that is worth having been done," he adds.

It really is remarkable how successful Obsidian was in following up such a celebrated release, and the very first RPG adaptation of Star Wars, with a game almost equally as beloved, all under pressure from the rights holder to deliver in an incredibly short timeframe. Just a couple of years later, the studio managed a similar feat with the release of Neverwinter Nights 2, yet another acclaimed RPG sequel to a BioWare-developed title. Leave it to Obsidian, I suppose.

#3864. Vote now for 2026's RPS 100: Reader Edition

For the past six years, the team at RPS have got together to pick what we consider to be the best 100 games you can play on PC. There's very little science involved, and we try not to get too hung up on what games should make the cut. From year to year, our rankings and choices vary wildly as the formation and tastes of the team changes.

However, our definitive list isn't always met with a chorus of approval and cheers of 'Hear, hear!', "'Well done!', and 'Couldn't have said it better myself!', so we also have the RPS 100: Reader Edition. This is your chance to submit your ten favourite PC games of all time. Your votes will be tallied up with all the other submissions from our other readers and we will produce a list of the community's top 100.

We've just finished revealing what we currently consider to be the Best PC games of all time and now it's your turn.

Using this very Google Form you can submit up to ten votes for your favourite PC games of all time. I will then tally them up with all the other votes from RPS's readers and produce a list of the community's top 100.

Now, a note on scoring. The game you put in 10th place will be awarded one point, 9th place will be worth two, 8th place will be worth three, and so on until you reach your top pick, which will be worth ten points. Please write the full game name (and include the year of release if there are multiple titles in a series with the same name, such as Doom (1993) and Doom (2016)). If in doubt, check how the game is titled on Steam.

Last year, I implemented a change to create a greater variety of games on the list. I combined series scores, so if one reader voted for Civilization IV and another voted for Civilization VI, the scores of both were combined and the entry would be for the Civilization series. I also shared the breakdown of the votes for each title in the entry, so you could see which was most popular within the series.

I will be doing the same again this year, as we saw a lot more games that wouldn't have made the cut otherwise. However, I will try to do a better job of separating out games that are very different from one another even if they are in the same series. Warcraft 3 and World of Warcraft are both Warcraft games, but, admittedly, they aren't similar games. I would ask for some leeway on this, though, as not every example is clear cut. Should Alpha Centauri be counted among the Civilization games? Are Final Fantasy XIV and Final Fantasy Tactics - The Ivalice Chronicles truly worlds away from the other games in the Final Fantasy series?

This does also mean that one-shot games can struggle to compete against games which are part of longrunning series. After all, Crimson Skies isn't just competing against Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020), it is competing against votes for any and all Microsoft Flight Simulator games ever released. Unfortunately, this is a cost of the system, but I prefer the variety that comes from seeing more games represented instead of several separate entries for games within the same series.

We also invite you to tell us why you've chosen each game. This is entirely voluntary, you can simply enter the game titles if you would prefer. However, I'll choose a selection of what readers have said about winning games so we can better understand why the RPS community loves these games. Try not to write any more than 100 words. If you have more to say you can always drop it in the comments of the list when we publish it at the end of the year.

To cast your votes, please make sure you complete this form by 5pm GMT on Sunday, December 6th.

Gravity Well, founded in 2020 as an "anti-crunch" game studio, lost its funding earlier this year and wasn't able to find a new backer.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Gravity Well, an "anti-crunch" studio founded in 2020 by former Apex Legends executive producer Drew McCoy and lead software engineer Jon Shiring, is entering "hibernation" after losing funding for its game.

Gravity Well's launch in 2020 came with high hopes. Founded by veterans of Call of Duty, Titanfall, and Apex Legends, it made the health of the team "an absolute top priority," McCoy said at the time.

"That means we are anti-crunch. That means good compensation. That means everyone at Gravity Well has creative freedom, because when someone else makes all of the decisions, work isn't fun and the end product isn't as good."

But like so many other ambitious new studios launched around that time, it fell victim to the post-pandemic retrenchment and has effectively shuttered without releasing a game. The shutdown comes just a month after the studio laid off more than 40 people in what it said was a "fight for survival" caused by the loss of funding. It also warned that "given the current state of the industry our future is uncertain."

A message now posted on the Gravity Well website (via RPS) says the funding situation hasn't changed, and "sadly the time has come for Gravity Well to go into hibernation."

"We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building," the message states. "Even moreso, the team we managed to cultivate was truly world class and we're going to miss getting to work with them every day. If you're a hiring manager or recruiter and a Gravity Well resume hits your desk they come with our highest recommendation."

The announcement concludes with an invitation to publishers and investors to reach out if they're interested in supporting the project.

Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill.
